observations.label: connected-announcement-1
observations.text:
You see a toll-rolls.

Bound crossing-counts under a rain-hood, a century
deep and mould-spotted: carts, heads, coin,
initials. One entry is pressed harder than the rest
of its year: short count -- forgiven -- my error.
The rolls do not record a face.
A fresh work slip reads: SELLA'S DRESSING SHELTER —
one stretch south of Sumphold. Bench brace broken:
two sound timber lengths needed. Old cutting works:
two stretches east of the shelter, beyond the
cutbank crossing. Keep to the dry bow if you can
spare the walk. Bring sumpsieve pads and knotflax
cord for wound dressings.

observations.label: connected-announcement-2
observations.text:
You see a dressing bench.
The dressing bench needs two salvaged timber before
it can be used. One sumpsieve pad, one knotflax
cord and two drams make one field dressing. Apply
it to treat existing ordinary poison and bleeding
together. It does not heal wounds or treat poison
gas or fungal infection.
The bench legs have split. The keeper cannot
tension a clean wrap on the loose frame. Brace it
with two sound timber lengths.
Repair: 2 salvaged timber. Composition: Wood.

A split-legged dressing bench with a cloth clamp
and a bitter-leaf press. Sella needs two sound
timber lengths to brace it. The abandoned cutting
works lie two stretches east, beyond the cutbank
crossing. Once repaired, the keeper wraps one
sumpsieve pad and one knotflax cord into a field
dressing for two drams. Dressings treat existing
ordinary poison and bleeding; they do not protect
against marsh gas.
